[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2021/08/20 (Fri) 19:52  
[EVENT] User is planning a trip to Costa Rica next year.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in birding spots and guides.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Costa Rica has over 850 bird species and is one of the most biodiverse countries in the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended birding spots include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Corcovado National Park - home to Resplendent Quetzal, Scarlet Macaw, and Harpy Eagle.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve - look for Resplendent Quetzal, Three-wattled Bellbird, and Bare-necked Umbrellabird.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Arenal Volcano National Park - ideal for Keel-billed Toucan, Great Curassow, and White Hawk.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Tortuguero Canals - spot Jabiru, Agami Heron, and White-fronted Nunbird.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Savegre Valley - hotspot for hummingbirds and species like Golden-browed Chlorophonia and Costa Rican Pygmy Owl.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended guides and tours include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Costa Rica Bird Observatories - offers guided birding tours and workshops.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Birding Costa Rica - guided birding tours with expert guides.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Tropical Birding - customized birding tours and photography workshops.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Costa Rica Gateway - a range of birding tours led by local guides.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Guides in Costa Rica - connects users with local birding guides.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Best time to visit is the dry season (December to April).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Consider eco-lodges or birding-oriented hotels.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Bring binoculars, a spotting scope, and a field guide.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Choose guides that follow responsible and sustainable tourism practices.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking forward to visiting the recommended places.
